To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
informal carers of dependent elderly people in the community have very little formal assistance, and that the burden of care falls disproportionately on women.
informal carers, especially the women, are under considerable strain, are often depressed and are often isolated.

1) the main source of care of the dependent elderly in the community is the family, usually the woman of the family, 2) the family carers of the elderly are not well supported, 3) the carers are distressed, have a poor quality of life and suffer psychological morbidity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the caring relationship and the consequences of that caring relationship for the carer.
the nature and extent of the informal care of the dependent elderly in the home, and with the consequences for the carers.
the nature and quality of life for the dependent elderly and their carers, and the implications for policy and practice of our findings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the family carers were not receiving the support they required to enable them to continue to look after their dependent relative at home.
there was a need for a more comprehensive service for those who care for their dependent elderly.
the carer of the dependent elderly has a great need for assistance and that this is not being met.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carers of the elderly are a neglected group.
the carers are not receiving enough help, either from the statutory or voluntary sector, and that the consequences of this are that the quality of their lives is impaired.
carers of the elderly are in need of help, but are not getting it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the family is a major resource and should be supported by a range of services.
the family is a vital resource for the care of the dependent elderly.
carers of the elderly are in need of more support.
